title: Leek, turnip and red lentil dal with halloumi

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple: leeks, turnips, kale, red lentils, tinned tomatoes, halloumi and dried spices.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including halloumi and garam masala, is an everyday line at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one large pan and a wooden spoon, and frying, softening and simmering are well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 250g red lentils in 900ml water plus a tin of tomatoes for 25 minutes gives a properly loose dal for four, with enough spice, kale and halloumi to make it a full meal.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes of active work covers slicing three leeks, dicing 400g of turnips, cubing the halloumi, frying it and softening the leeks, and the 25-minute simmer plus 5 minutes for the kale matches the 30 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming dal suits mid-December, and three leeks softened as the base are a central part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, three vegetables and halloumi make a filling, balanced family dinner.
